description_en: A place (gāḥ) in Jawalakhel is the final destination of the Buṅgadyaḥ chariot. Jāvalākhela Phalcā 1 is located to the south of this place. The chariot remains in front of the Phalcā for four days before finally being dismantled. From the day that the chariot reaches Jawalakhel until the day of Bhotojātrā (i.e. the last day of the months-long procession), the Matsyendranātha Mṛdaṅga Bhajana Khalaḥ recite hymns in Jāvalākhela Phalcā every morning and evening. During the chariot's time in Jawalakhel, pilgrims come to the Phalcā and light lamps in the name of Buṅgadyaḥ. When the Bhoṭo (the jewel-studded vest of Lord Rato Machhindranath, the God of rains and good harvest) is exhibited, the Kumārī of Patan also visits Jāvalākhela Phalcā. It appears that no land or property has been provided for the Phalcā. There is a stone inscription embedded in the south wall of Jāvalākhela Phalcā, however it is illegible.Although listed as a single Phalcā, Jāvalākhela Phalcā appears to really made up of two three-bayphalcāsthat have been joined together to make a five-bay structure. This presumption is supported by the fact that the building has been divided by a brick wall and two, rather than one, columns are placed at its center. Aphalcāwith an even number of bays (e.g. 6-bays) is considered to be inauspicious; no other example of a Phalcā with six bays is known to exist in the Kathmandu Valley. The eastern half has large edge stones while the western half has been built with a new timber edge.Jāvalākhela Phalcā retains six historic carved blind windows above its six bays. The timber roof framing is entirely new, however historic hand-made tiles (jhingati) have been used to cover the roof.Two makeshift tea-shops have been set up on either side of Jāvalākhela Phalcā and customers can find shelter from rain and sun here. The left half also serves as the sleeping quarters of one of the teashop owners. A woman called 'Rādhā Devī' has been running her tea shop in the eastern wing of the Phalcā for several decades now. She also sleeps there overnight.According to local informants, Jāvalākhela Phalcā was rebuilt from the ground up not long before the 2015 earthquakes struck. All of the facing bricks, decorative bricks and paving tiles (telya) are new. The left half of the Phalcā retains its three large historic edge stones on the upper platform. Seven of the ten pillars and capitals are historic and heavily worn. Their varying sizes and carving styles indicate that some were reused from otherphalcās.
description_ne: जावलाखेलमा बुङ्गद्यःको रथ अन्तिम पटक रोकिने स्थान (गाः) रहेको छ । उक्त स्थान नजिकै दक्षिणमा यो फल्चा बनेको छ । छ कवल भएको फल्चाको बीच भागमा भित्ता बनाई कवलहरु विभाजन गरिएको छ । जावलाखेलमा बुङ्गद्यःको रथ आइपुगेको दिनबाट भोटोजात्राको दिनसम्म फल्चामा मत्सेन्द्रनाथ भजन खलःले विहान-बेलुकी भजन गर्दै आएको छ । रथ जावलाखेल पुगेदेखी बुङ्गद्यःको नाममा १०८को संख्यामा दियो बाल्न आउने भक्तजनबाट फल्चामा बसी दियो बाल्ने गरेको पाइन्छ तर भजनको समयमा भने फल्चा खाली गरिन्छ । बुङ्गद्यःको भोटो देखाइने समय पाटन कुमारीलाई यसै फल्चामा उपस्थित गराइन्छ । फल्चासंग सम्बन्धित कुनै गुथि अस्तित्वमा छैन । भोटोजात्राको दिनमा भने गुठी संस्थानले फल्चामा रङ्गरोगन गर्ने तथा नयाँ इलां राख्ने कार्य गर्दे आएको छ ।फल्चाको दक्षिणी भित्तामा एक शिलापत्र टाँसिएर राखिएको छ तर शिलापत्र पूर्ण रुपमा खिइसकेकाले कुनै जानकारी भने पाउन सकिएको छैन ।
brick_type: dāci apā (conical veneer brick), mā apā (regular fired brick)
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths), Repaired

historical_events.event_description: Local informants agreed that the Phalcā was restored shortly before the 2015 earthquakes, however a precise date could not be ascertained. The Municipality has no details on record.
The surface of the stone inscription embedded in the southern wall is severely damaged. Only a few characters of the inscription are legible.
